PullRequest.Title: chat: add Blobby jump game
PullRequest.Body:

Splits the Blobby game out of #343630 so the landing regression can be reviewed and merged independently. This PR excludes the clean-landing fix and its tests. No tracking issue.

## Changes

- Activate the pet on the new-session welcome heading to play, or choose **Play Jump Game** from its context menu while it is on the normal input surface. Keyboard entry works with reduced motion enabled.
- Hold Space to charge, release to jump, and use Left/Right to hop or aim. Reachable random platforms, a pet-following camera, a pixel-art charge gauge, and reversible fades leave the normal new-session layout and draft unchanged.
- Introduce progressively narrower ledges, moving platforms from platform 5, crumbling platforms from platform 9, and wall-bank challenges from platform 12 where the course has room. Moving platforms carry Blobby; crumbling platforms provide a charge window before falling; wall impacts preserve the reflected jump angle.
- Show **Hops** in the top-right with **High score** underneath. A new highest-platform landing earns one hop; returning to old platforms does not farm points. The best run is saved locally on the device, while each new run starts at zero.
- Return to normal collision/respawn behavior when falling out of the game or returning to typing. Cancel undersized playfields during relayout before the pet or controls clip.
- Preserve pause ownership through accessible-view symbol/keybinding pickers, release it on genuine abandonment without stealing focus, and describe hazards and scores in accessibility help/current-state content.
- Include focused physics, gameplay, storage, keyboard, and lifecycle regressions. No component fixtures.

## Try it

Enable Blobby with `/vscode-pet`. Focus him with Tab, press Shift+F10, choose **Play Jump Game**, and press Enter. Alternatively, drag him onto the welcome heading and activate him. Try partial/full charges, directional jumps, and falling off. Moving ledges have arrow markings; broken-line ledges crumble after landing. On wall sections, aim into the wall to bank onto the narrow ledge.

Watch Hops increase on new highest-platform landings, exit with Escape, and start another run: Hops should reset while High score remains. Open the game's accessibility help or Accessible View and use its pickers; gameplay and platform timers stay paused during supported round-trips. Clicking into the input or typing fades out the game and drops the pet onto normal surfaces. The existing draft and layout should be preserved.

Live Code OSS Agents-window checks also passed: a 14-hop keyboard-driven course through moving, crumbling, and bank-shot sections; high-score persistence across renderer reload; and high-contrast HUD/platform visibility. A separate captioned demo recorded all 7 scenario steps successfully, including the wall-bank landing and high-score reset behavior. The recording is local and is not attached to this PR.

Full smoke/integration suites and manual screen-reader testing were not run. Hosted CI results are separate from these local checks.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The model appends every generated platform and never removes one, while the fixed 120 Hz physics loop and 60 Hz renderer explicitly iterate the complete arrays. The linear mechanism and hot-path reachability are certain; only how long typical users pursue high scores before the growth becomes noticeable is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU iterations and square-root collision calculations over retained platform objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: After reaching N platforms, airborne gameplay performs roughly 120N platform-state visits plus 120N collision tests per second, and rendering adds about 60N visibility tests per second; N only increases for the lifetime of the run.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: steadily increasing frame CPU time, lower rendering throughput, and eventual gameplay jank in long high-score runs
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The product had no jump-game course or per-frame physics scans before this PR, so chat idle/input paths did not retain and revisit an ever-growing platform history.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new course generator appends platforms indefinitely, and line 342 tests every retained platform for every fixed physics substep even though only platforms crossing the player's short vertical trajectory can collide; separate new loops also update and render-scan the full history.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added `ensurePlatforms` lines 153/181 only push onto `_platforms`; added line 342 loops over all `_platforms` inside `step()`, which `advance()` runs at 120 Hz, while browser line 252 independently scans all model platforms each animation frame.
Findings.Title: Bound platform collision scans as the course grows
Findings.Impact: A player pursuing an extended high-score run accumulates hundreds or thousands of old platforms; even when only a handful are visible or near the player, all old platforms continue consuming physics and render CPU every frame, so controls and animation progressively stutter.
Findings.Evidence: The array is height-ordered and monotonically extended by `ensurePlatforms`, with no pruning or index. `step()` first loops over all platforms at line 267 and, while airborne, line 342 loops over all of them again and calls `crossingTime` (including `Math.sqrt`) for each. The requestAnimationFrame renderer also traverses the complete array merely to reject offscreen entries. Tests exercise generation only to bounded heights/16 hops and do not establish a runtime cap.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve lower-platform landing semantics but index the height-ordered platforms and query only the current trajectory/viewport range; track moving and actively crumbling platforms separately (or compute their phase lazily) so offscreen history is not revisited at 120 Hz.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new requestAnimationFrame loop is explicit, and render writes layout-affecting left/top/width styles for visible platforms before synchronously reading overlay geometry on every active frame. During jumps those values change continuously, so the read-after-write flush is not speculative; exact cost varies with browser and workbench size.
Findings.PerformanceResource: synchronous DOM style recalculation and layout work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The forced flush occurs once per rendered gameplay frame (typically 60 times per second) after mutations to every visible platform and wall; its cost grows with the dirty DOM/layout subtree.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: extra main-thread layout passes and dropped animation frames during jumps
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no jump-game animation loop, no per-frame platform style mutation, and no overlay geometry read on this path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added render loop mutates platform and wall geometry, then calls getBoundingClientRect on the overlay before applying pet and gauge writes, splitting one animation frame into a forced layout followed by another set of invalidating writes.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 306 reads `this.overlay.getBoundingClientRect()` after added lines 252-305 have assigned layout-affecting `left`, `top`, `width`, and `height` styles; added `scheduleFrame` calls `render()` and reschedules itself every animation frame.
Findings.Title: Move the overlay geometry read before frame writes
Findings.Impact: While the jump game is active, especially during camera movement, the renderer can force an avoidable synchronous layout every frame and then invalidate layout again, consuming frame budget and making animation/input visibly stutter on slower or layout-heavy workbenches.
Findings.Evidence: `scheduleFrame()` executes `render()` on each requestAnimationFrame. In `render`, visible platform and wall positions/sizes are written first, then line 306 synchronously requests geometry, and pet/gauge positions are written afterward. On airborne frames camera height changes all visible platform tops, guaranteeing dirty layout before the read.
Findings.Recommendation: Cache the overlay-to-bounds offset during `layout()`/game setup, or perform the overlay geometry read at the start of the frame before any DOM writes, then batch all style updates afterward.

Scenarios.Scenario: Play the Blobby jump game and climb an extended course
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each focused gameplay frame synchronously advances the fixed-step model, renders all course collections, performs DOM geometry/style work, and schedules the next frame. On a new highest-platform landing, score persistence also runs inside render before the frame completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronous DOM geometry read (`getBoundingClientRect`) after layout-affecting platform/wall writes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per active animation frame, after writes to each visible platform/wall; normally about 60 reads/second.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No jump-game frame loop or this read-after-write DOM boundary existed before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Forces pending style/layout before pet and gauge writes, adding another main-thread layout phase to the gameplay frame.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and persist the device-local high score through `IStorageService`
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read at game start and whenever score/storage changes; one store for each newly exceeded high score, effectively at most once per newly reached highest platform.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No jump-game score key was read or written before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Invoked synchronously from render on a scoring landing, but cardinality is one per hop rather than per frame and storage service owns persistence batching; evidence does not establish a reportable regression by itself.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is the highest generated platform count N for the current run. Generation is height ordered and deduplicated by platform ID, but platforms/walls are never evicted; only the DOM-node maps are limited to currently visible entries. Physics performs approximately 240N platform visits/second while airborne and rendering adds approximately 60N visibility visits/second.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single recursively scheduled requestAnimationFrame drives the game, so frames do not intentionally overlap. `advance` serializes fixed 120 Hz substeps and caps one delayed frame to 100 ms (up to 12 substeps), but there is no limiter or index bounding work by course history. Window blur/focus ownership makes concurrent active games unlikely; no worker offload is used.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold start reads the saved high score, generates the initial lookahead course, and creates visible DOM nodes. Warm frames reuse visible platform/wall DOM nodes through maps, but there is no range cache/index for model arrays, so old platforms are rescanned forever. The high score is positive state in application storage and is updated on cross-window storage changes; there is no miss-retry issue.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the requestAnimationFrame call path, read-after-write ordering, 120 Hz fixed-step loops, monotonic array growth, and lack of pruning/indexing are explicit in added code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The per-frame forced layout is immediate, but exact duration depends on browser/layout subtree size. Course-scan growth is certain, while the number of users sustaining hundreds or thousands of hops and the hardware threshold for visible jank are uncertain; this is reflected in low severity for that finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: Two reportable regressions: every gameplay frame can force a synchronous layout between write batches, and CPU work grows linearly with all platforms ever generated rather than the visible/collision range.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start the game from the welcome perch or pet context menu, then relayout/resize the Agents window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Activation discovers a visible jump-game platform, reads movement/pet/platform bounds, constructs the model and game DOM, moves the overlay, performs `layout`, focuses the pet, and starts the first frame. ResizeObserver/platform-change callbacks synchronously call game `layout`; an undersized playfield exits instead.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: DOM visibility and geometry reads for host platforms, movement bounds, pet, stage, and effects
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A handful on activation; several reads per coalesced resize/platform-change event, plus O(N) model resize updates for generated course objects.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The pet already measured ordinary platforms, but the PR adds jump-game eligibility reads and full game-stage layout/model resize on this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All reads and resize updates must complete before game start or relayout can render, but normal platform cardinality is small and resize frequency is bounded by UI events.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Platform discovery scans the host's deduplicated platform elements, realistically the input plus a small number of welcome/session controls. Layout resizes every generated platform/wall, so relayout cost also scales with course history N, but relayout frequency is event-driven rather than per frame.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Activation and relayout execute serially on the UI thread. ResizeObserver delivery coalesces browser resize changes, and the widget keeps one `ChatPetJumpGame` instance; no parallel IPC, subprocess, network, or filesystem work occurs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: DOM platform bounds are freshly measured on each discovery/layout; no geometry cache is retained across host changes. Existing generated course/model objects are reused on warm relayouts. Invalid/undersized geometry cancels the game rather than retaining a failed allocation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for call path and cardinality; moderate for real-world resize frequency because ResizeObserver/browser coalescing is environment dependent.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Host platform count is small in the supplied new-session UI; resize storms and very long courses can increase work, but no separate high-confidence regression beyond the reported active-frame/history mechanisms was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: activation is one-shot and normal relayout cardinality is bounded; history-dependent model resizing is covered by the broader unbounded course-work finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open accessibility help/current-state view and traverse symbol or keybinding pickers during gameplay
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The provider snapshots local game content, pauses the game by cancelling its frame handle, and opens the accessible view. Nested help/pickers transfer provider disposal ownership; closing resumes one frame loop, while replacement/abandonment disposes the game path without restoring focus.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Content generation scans the retained platform array to filter/slice four nearby platforms and scans walls to slice three. Invocation is user-triggered and the animation is paused, so this O(N) scan does not repeat per frame. Provider/picker ownership remains one active chain.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Pause clears the sole scheduled frame before view work. Quick picks and providers are replaced serially through `MutableDisposable`; tests cover selection, cancellation, replacement, blur, and disposal. No concurrent network, IPC, subprocess, filesystem, or database operation is reached.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Accessible content is a fresh snapshot with no cache, appropriate because game state changes between invocations. Pause/resume state is transferred through provider disposal rather than duplicated. Repeated picker transitions reuse no expensive remote result and clean prior disposables.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: provider construction, pause/resume, disposal transfer, and picker tests establish lifecycle behavior and absence of repeating external boundaries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very long runs make the one-shot content filters O(N), but the game is paused and output is capped to four platforms/three walls, so user-visible cost is unlikely before the already reported continuous history scans dominate.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: work is local and user-triggered, the frame loop is paused, and changed lifecycle code prevents duplicate animation or retained picker/provider resources.

Scenarios.Scenario: Exit, blur, type, disable, or switch hosts while the game/fade is active
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Exit captures current pet geometry, optionally starts a 160 ms compositor animation, disposes the game (cancelling frame/listeners and restoring the overlay), and either restores the perch or hands the pet to existing fall/landing physics. Immediate exits clear pending fade/fall layers first.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: DOM geometry reads and overlay reparenting during exit/fall handoff
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A few reads/reparents once per exit, restart, disable, or host switch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No jump-game overlay or fade/fall handoff existed before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to preserve visual position before existing fall physics can continue; one-shot and bounded.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One game layer, one frame disposable, one optional fade animation, visible DOM maps, and one fall-layer disposable per exit. Cleanup clears all maps/nodes at once; cost is proportional to currently visible DOM nodes, not all retained model platforms.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: MutableDisposable replacement serializes game, exit animation, and fall-layer ownership. Restart/disable/dispose paths clear prior resources before creating or completing another path; no unbounded timer or animation concurrency remains.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No exited game/model is cached. Fade nodes are retained only until animation finish/cancel (160 ms) and then removed; reduced motion/hidden documents dispose immediately. Persistent high score survives by design, while run course state does not.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High based on explicit disposable ownership and focused lifecycle tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser animation cancellation ordering varies, but cleanup tests cover restart, host switch, disable, disposal, blur, and reduced motion; no evidence of retained resources or repeated cleanup cost remains.
Scenarios.Verdict: No cleanup-lifecycle finding: frame, animation, listeners, DOM layers, and focus ownership are bounded and released across abandonment paths.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 19 changed files and paginated diffs. Reported one per-frame synchronous-layout regression and one course-history CPU-scaling regression; startup, relayout, accessibility, persistence, and cleanup paths were traced without additional reportable issues.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
